idiom_name: DAO class over JetBrains Exposed (Database.connect + transaction { Table.selectAll() })
implementation_notes: Kotlin's dominant realization is Exposed, JetBrains' Kotlin SQL framework: Database.connect() creates the database object, tables are declared as objects extending Table, and each operation runs inside transaction { } using the DSL with type-safe column references, so the DAO owns the transaction boundary and the table definitions while callers see only Kotlin types. What is library-provided is SQL construction and the JDBC plumbing; what the DAO still adds is the domain vocabulary and the ResultRow-to-data-class mapping. Spring Data JPA with Kotlin data classes is the equivalent alternative when the domain is already JPA-mapped.
pitfalls: ResultRow values are valid only inside their transaction: work returned out of the block must be materialised into data classes, and blocking JDBC calls inside a coroutine belong on Dispatchers.IO.
Table objects are global singletons bound to one name and one database connection registry, so a second store cannot reuse them silently and name collisions surface only at query time.
transaction { } swallows nothing but commits on normal exit only: an exception thrown after a partial write rolls back the whole block, so keep each DAO method's transactional scope deliberate.
